newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania opposition warns of more protests.
newsitem.headline: Albania opposition warns of more protests.

text.p: Albania's main opposition party on Monday slammed President Sali Berisha's government for breaking up a weekend demonstration and reiterated its determination to hold further protests.
The demonstrators were led by angry investors desperate to retrieve their life savings from crumbling get-rich-quick pyramid schemes, blaming the government for doing nothing to regulate them.

Leaders of the main opposition Socialist Party, the former communists, said they intended to inform all Western governments and international organisations of the "grave situation" in Albania, for which they blamed the ruling Democratic Party.
"The popular protest...called for the dismissal of this discredited government, it was a political protest against the current economic collapse," a Socialist party statement said.
In a desperate attempt to offset their losses, many disillusioned Albanians turned on Monday to television bingo in the hope of making some quick money.
"I lost all the money I had deposited into Sude's (pyramid) company, and Tele-bingo is my last chance," said a woman after buying some 30 tickets at a kiosk.
The Sude pyramid scheme, once one of the most popular, collapsed last week.
Berisha vowed at the weekend to crack down on the pyramid schemes but warned the opposition against exploiting anger among investors to try to destabilise the ex-communist state.

But thousands ignored his warning on Sunday and turned out to protest against the government for doing little to regulate the pyramid schemes, which promised huge returns from small investments but have wiped out many people's life savings.
The demonstrators, led by opposition leaders, stormed through police cordons to Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square, scene of a 1990 uprising that toppled the former hardline communist regime.
The government has banned protesters from the square, which was also the site of demonstrations last year against alleged vote-rigging by the Democrats in a general election.
"The Socialist Party is convinced all the Albanian people will continue to protest. (It) will be at the head of these peaceful protests," the statement continued.
The party rejected an interior ministry announcement accusing the opposition of encouraging people to daub themselves with red ink in order to fake injury.
It cited the complaint of one protester Syrja Bebri, 58, who said he had suffered injury after being beaten on the head by a police baton.
The Socialists voiced concern over the arrest of a number of protesters in Tirana and in the southern town of Fier, and warned the government it would be responsible if the situation worsened.
